coordinatorSummary: ACCEPT at 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX, with 2 advisories. Twenty-two attacks run, none landed. Custody holds: subject ba042987 at 0444, 11662 bytes, unmoved at both ends; HEAD never left 5d5d778; live required-now 26 of 26; file 08 and COORD unmodified. All eight cited digests reproduce, COORD among them pinned at the live value so no append-only argument is needed, and recordedInputs.HEAD equals the top-level head as the artifact's own clause requires. The live DR-122 token is PROPOSED-CLOSED-FOR-REVIEW and the subject states exactly that rather than defaulting to the OPEN its siblings carry. The dispatch's sharpest test passes cleanly: fixtureClassesVerbatim equals v15's live fixtureClasses as an ordered list of six id-and-previewStanding pairs — same order, same ids, same standings, no mismatch — and the ACTIVE trio and INACTIVE trio partition into the two obligations sorted-equal, with leftoverDesign true on the ACTIVE side and false on the INACTIVE side. Nothing ACTIVE was parked as deferred and nothing INACTIVE was pulled forward. Completeness is unusually checkable here: v15 has no namedOpenDecisions key and zero unauthored markers outside its fixture classes, so those six are its whole unauthored surface and the join covers all six. All eight of v15's whatThisDoesNotDo items land, three of them near-verbatim in the subject's own doesNot. All four cited verdicts are exact, including the dual ACCEPT 0/0 D-115 records. The advisory identifiers looked wrong at first — the Claude review's own id is ADV-1, not CLAUDE-V15-ADV-1 — and I traced provenance before reporting, as the same shape misled me toward a false finding on the packaging join: D-115 applies a qualify-rename discipline, 'advisory ADV-1 (qualify CLAUDE-V15-ADV-1)', and the adopted COORD sentence names all three ids, which the subject reproduces with attribution. Refuted. The DR-131 boundary holds, and it holds in a way worth noting: unlike the DR-105 and DR-120 joins, this one does not flip a harness-spec authoring obligation even though G26 v1 exists with a verified Claude ACCEPT 0/0, because file 08 ties G26's corpus to DR-131 NT-5 and the close belongs there. That restraint is the correct call, not a gap. Two advisories, neither barring acceptance. The first is that file 08 still calls the G26 harness not authored — the third row in this family after DR-G09 and DR-G15 — though it is weaker here than in the siblings, because this subject asserts no authoring close and so neither creates nor engages the disagreement; the correction is owed by whichever cycle records G26 on DR-131. The second is that the quoted D-115 sentence calls SARIFV15-A1 a Claude advisory when it is the Codex one, which I established by reading the advisory ids out of both pinned reviews; the subject is faithfully quoting an adopted recording and attributes it, so it stays advisory, but the sentence is being copied forward and the fix is one word. I also tested the omitted-obligation shape that produced findings on the two prior joins — v15's four identity dependencies, of which the subject cites two — and it did not land: the two cited are the ones that drive the INACTIVE classification, while ID-DEP-S3 rides an already-applied D9 golden that blocks nothing and ID-DEP-S4 is a DR-111 admission question that changes no DR-122 leftover. One disclosure: I opened the v15 Codex verdict, reading only its verdict line, counts and advisory id, to check a load-bearing citation and to establish the lane in advisory A2; a coordinator reading the prohibition strictly should discount that one verification.
